speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. Can you tell me exactly where it hurts when you try to walk, and does the pain get worse at night or while you are resting?

speaker: Patient
text: 7-year-old male. Mother has noticed a change in the child’s play patterns, specifically favoring his left leg while walking or running. The child complains of pain in his left knee, but denies any recent trauma or injury. He has no fever or other systemic symptoms. Nutrition and developmental milestones are appropriate for age.

speaker: Doctor
text: I understand the pain is in the left knee, but can you tell me if pressing on the joint itself hurts, or if the pain is actually higher up in your thigh? Also, has anyone noticed any swelling or redness in that area?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Pain localized to the left knee. I also have Limping favoring left leg, No fever, No systemic symptoms.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Transient Synovitis of the Left Hip (presenting as referred knee pain)

*Note: While the patient reports knee pain, in pediatric patients, hip pathology such as transient synovitis or early Legg-Calvé-Perthes disease often presents with knee discomfort. The absence of fever makes septic arthritis less likely, and the lack of trauma makes a fracture unlikely. Further imaging is required to confirm the source of pain and rule out avascular necrosis.*

REQUEST IMAGES: Pelvic_X-Ray (AP and Frog-leg lateral)
